stance.label: Short-term bearish, leverage flushed; long-term in the bottom zone

headline: The stab to $55K flushed leverage, and spot buyers have not taken over; the prior low held on the close and faces a retest at Monday's US open.
summary: Short-term bearish, with one layer of selling gone: the intraday drop to $55,100 swept the estimated long-liquidation band, the close recovered to $60,089 and funding sits near zero. Long-term bullish: long-term holders are selling at an average 23% loss, the largest capitulation of this cycle, with valuation in the historical bottom zone. A close below $58,525 is a new cycle low; a turn needs ETF and stablecoin outflows to stop, and Monday's US stock open is the first test.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 10 straight closes below; the close needs +20.5% to get back above

overview.lead: No ETFs and no US stocks on a Saturday, so crypto drew this long lower wick alone; the real test is Monday's US open.
points: Intraday low $55,100, 5.9% under the June 30 closing low; the close got back above $60K after a 9.8% daily range.
Volume ran 1.5x the 20-day average, a third less than the day before; Fear & Greed 12, ninth day of extreme fear.
November to date −22.4%; the worst November since 2013 was 2018's −37.0%.
The exit framework took no new action today and the market-stage label is unchanged.

cycle.lead: The long-term cheapness is intact; what loosened is the premise that June was the most painful point: the share of long-term holders at a loss hit a new high for this cycle.
points: Long-term holder loss share reached 46.5% on Nov 20, above this cycle's prior high of 45.4%; in the last three cycles it never made a new high after the bottom, and this time it did (CheckOnChain).
Price traded through $58,525 intraday but did not close below it; Tidemark's cycle-low hypothesis is still under test (its data runs to Nov 20), deadline Dec 19, bottom signal 39.6, short of 50.
Market stage is still bull, with 3 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA; the rule needs 30 to exit. Only 1 of 6 supporting lights is on (exchange supply).
The weekly bull-bear score is more negative than last week while the Dawn Index sits in Deep Night. Trend points down, valuation says cheap, and the two gauges are telling different stories.

market.lead: The down leg is not over; this is just the first time someone bought price back off a low. A close above $67,627 would turn it into an up leg.
points: 61 days since Sep 21, −30.6% on a closing basis, deepest −32.1% on Nov 20; bigger than 92% of the 12 down legs in this cycle.
Price pierced the −2 standard deviation line of the short-term holder cost band at $56,745 intraday and closed back at −1.65 standard deviations (Bitview).
Sell Pressure Index maxed for a 12th day, momentum at 0.08; this combination has occurred 20 times since 2012, with 12 gains after 90 days and a median further drop of 12% before exit.

The thickest bucket above the close is $62,000 with 387K BTC; 127K BTC moved into the $64,000 bucket over 7 days, so a bounce into this area meets coins that just changed price level (Bitview; on-chain moves are not necessarily trades).

deriv.lead: The bounce came from liquidations ending plus short covering: perps loosened while options tightened.
points: This page's two findings are two sides of the same day: the estimated long-liquidation band at $55.2–57.0K was swept by the intraday low, with $275M of longs and $137M of shorts liquidated on the day (Coinalyze).
OI-weighted funding 0.08%, with shorts paying on OKX (−4.1%) and Bybit (−1.2%); open interest down 4.4% in 7 days, yet 77.7% of Binance accounts are still long.
DVOL 58.0, the highest since Mar 8; 7-day implied vol is 9.2 points above 90-day, 25Δ risk reversal −12.7, and buyer premium has leaned to puts for 24 days.

The estimated liquidation bands switched sides: 27.5K BTC of shorts at $65.4–67.8K above, about 8K BTC of longs at $53.7–55.1K below (multiple exchanges, estimated); the order book shows $240M of asks at $60,000 and $154M of bids at $59,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: The money has not come back: stablecoins keep getting redeemed, the USDT discount fell into its deepest 5% of the last four years, and US spot is still net selling.
points: The Nov 20 ETF figure is −$127M, but IBIT's creations and redemptions for that day are not out yet (CoinDesk, Nov 21; Farside shows −$124.5M with the IBIT column blank), so the full picture of the crash day waits for Monday.
Stablecoins at $282.5B, down 1.6% in 7 days and $19.0B in 30 days (DefiLlama); USDT at $0.9979, with a 7-day average discount of 0.136%.
Coinbase spot net taker selling of 5,878 BTC over 7 days, still at the lowest since August 2021; the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount is −0.01%, so the US and offshore are about even.

Asia still points the other way: Korea premium 2.6%, Asian OTC USDT premium 0.72%. Today (Nov 22) is the echo date of last year's suspected wallet move in apparent demand, so the −315K BTC reading is not treated as weaker demand for these few days.

onchain.lead: Loss-taking has not stopped, it is just smaller than the day before; long-term holders realized $4.36B of losses in 7 days, the biggest week of this cycle.
points: Long-term holder 7-day realized loss equals 0.361% of market cap versus 0.292% on June 30; the LTH-SOPR 7-day average of 0.773 is the lowest since June 30 (Bitview).
Network-wide realized loss was $1.88B on the day, 15.6 basis points of market cap versus 24 the day before; price went lower intraday and loss-taking did not grow with it.

Short-term holders are in a 12th day of concentrated capitulation, intensity 4.03; they realized 15,352 BTC of losses and 2,056 BTC of profit on the day, and STH-SOPR has been below 1 for 16 days (CheckOnChain).
By address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 70K BTC in 7 days while the 1K–10K tier shed 47K BTC; the close is back 0.9% above estimated production cost.

exit.lead: No new framework action today: an intraday break of the prior low is not a framework condition, and the hedge buy-back condition was already met on Nov 17.
points: 10 straight closes below the 200-day MA at $72,428, 17.0% under it.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.398, with the 0.75 line at $110,893; the three top indicators read 5 / 5 / 24, all low (CoinMetrics, Nov 20).

news.title: BTC rebounds more than 9% from a two-year low of $55,130 and retakes $60,000; about $1.8B of crypto positions liquidated in 24 hours, $1.3B of them longs (CoinGlass)
news.read: Our Kraken intraday low is $55,100 and the close $60,089; Coinalyze shows $275M of longs and $137M of shorts liquidated on the day, same direction, and the two vendors' totals are not netted against each other. QCP, quoted in the piece, says short-covering rallies struggle to last, and we also see spot net taker selling on the day. Short-term noise with a slight positive tilt; it does not change the cycle view.

news.title: US stocks for the week: S&P 500 −8.6%, Dow −8%, Nasdaq −10%; the Nasdaq is now down 2.7% for the year
news.read: BTC's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.66; since Sep 21 BTC is down 30.6% and the Nasdaq 12.0% (Nasdaq through Nov 19). Saturday's bounce happened with US stocks closed; if tech sells off again at Monday's open (22:30 Taipei, 14:30 UTC), the prior low at $58,525 gets tested again. It does not change the cycle view.

news.title: Spot BTC ETFs show a provisional $124.5M net outflow for Nov 20, flagged as incomplete; Nov 19 was −$582M, about −$541M of it from IBIT (CoinGlass, SoSoValue)
news.read: Our CoinMarketCap figure for Nov 20 is −$126.8M, so the two match, but neither includes IBIT yet; IBIT alone was 93% of the prior day's outflow, so treat this number as a floor. The last 20 trading days total −$3.67B, still inside an outflow stretch. Until Monday's complete figure, the reading that ETFs barely sold on the crash day does not stand.

news.title: CryptoQuant: BTC holders realized more than $11.3B of losses in 7 days, about 8x the profits booked in the same period; Glassnode: the largest estimated long-liquidation cluster at $59,000–62,000 has been cleared
news.read: Our Bitview series shows $12.28B of realized losses over 7 days, with 7-day profits only 0.115x losses, so direction and scale agree across vendors. Glassnode says that cluster is cleared; our next estimated long band sits at $53.7–55.1K and is much smaller. Losses this large support the bottom-zone case, but with buyers still absent it is too early to call the decline over.

news.title: BTC drops below $57,000, the lowest since September 2024; about $2.4B of crypto futures liquidated in 24 hours, over $1B in BTC and $545M in ETH; gold falls to its lowest since September 2025
news.read: The report puts the cause on rising real yields and a hawkish Fed, with gold and tech falling together. Our 10-year real yield is 2.88%, up 12 bp over 20 trading days (Nov 19); since Sep 21 gold is down 18.7% and BTC 30.6%. Every non-yielding asset is being sold at once, and the flows backdrop will not help before the Dec 9 decision.

news.title: US close on Nov 20: Nasdaq −5.28%, Nvidia −14%, Anthropic −8.5% on its second trading day; money moved into Treasuries as a haven and yields fell
news.read: Yesterday's coverage was about stocks; the new part today is bonds: money hid in Treasuries and yields eased, which takes a little pressure off non-yielding assets. Our 2-year yield is 4.63%, 0.63 points above the policy-rate ceiling; Polymarket prices a December hike at 91.6% versus 96.2% a week ago. Hike expectations eased only slightly, short of changing the flows backdrop.

news.title: Strategy shares fell 22.8% in a week (Nov 13–Nov 19 closes); it leaves MSCI indexes after the Nov 30 close, with index funds estimated to sell up to 13M shares; Monness Crespi cut it to Sell
news.read: We show Strategy holding 850,848 BTC at a −20.4% paper loss (CoinGecko). The stock is falling faster than the coin, which narrows the issue-shares-to-buy-BTC path; it bought only 485 BTC in the week of Nov 9–15. What goes missing is a steady buyer, the same direction as ETFs and stablecoins; trading below cost does not mean forced selling.

actions.head: No action today.
actions.text: No new trigger: the hedge buy-back condition was met on Nov 17, and the MVRV Z 7-day average is 0.31, still below 0.5 (CoinMetrics, Nov 20).

actions.head: Do not read one long lower wick as a confirmed bottom.
actions.text: The wick shows shorts covered once liquidations ended; it does not show new money: spot was net taker selling on the day and option protection got pricier. After the big June 2 liquidation, price fell another 12% before the June 30 low.

actions.head: $58,525: broken intraday, not on the close.
actions.text: A close below it is a new cycle low (Tidemark's test runs to Dec 19); the estimated long-liquidation band below is $53.7–55.1K, and under that the realized price at $53,206 (Bitview). The first hurdle above is the thick supply at $62,000–64,000.

actions.head: Monday's US stock open (Nov 23, 22:30 Taipei, 14:30 UTC) and the complete Nov 20 ETF figure.
actions.text: The Nasdaq fell 10% last week; IBIT's Nov 20 flows are still unpublished. October PCE and the Q3 GDP revision land Nov 25 at 21:30 Taipei (13:30 UTC), US markets close Nov 26 for Thanksgiving, and the Deribit monthly expiry is Nov 27 at 16:00 Taipei (08:00 UTC) with 26.7% of open interest and max pain at $73,000, too far from spot to be a reliable pull.

actions.head: The next things that would move the framework are the MVRV 0.75 line at $110,893 and the $125,000 level.
actions.text: They are 84.5% and 108.0% away, both far; the close is 17.0% under the 200-day MA at $72,428.

changes.title: The crash-day ETF outflow looks small, but IBIT is missing
changes.say: IBIT was 93% of the prior day's outflow, so a number without it cannot be used to say selling eased; the last 20 trading days total −$3.67B.

changes.title: The 30-day rise in open interest is gone
changes.say: Price fell 26% in 30 days and open interest only now returned to where it was 30 days ago; leverage has started to leave, though not by much.

changes.title: The USDT discount crossed the deep-discount line
changes.fig: 7-day average discount 0.115% → 0.136% (line at 0.119%); $0.9979 on the day
changes.say: People are converting stablecoins back to dollars, the same story as shrinking stablecoin supply. Past spells below this line were followed by mixed 30-day returns; direction depends on when redemptions slow.

changes.title: The close is back above estimated production cost
changes.say: It spent a single day below. Hashrate rose 14.4% in a week and difficulty is set to rise another 9.0% on Nov 27, so breakeven keeps climbing and one day does not ease the pressure on miners.

findings.title: $55K swept leveraged longs; what bought it back was not spot demand
findings.lean_why: A block of forced long selling below is gone and shorts are now the more crowded side above, removing one downward push; spot buying did not follow, so the bounce lacks staying power.
findings.what: The leg through the prior low was driven by liquidations: the low of $55,100 swept the estimated long-liquidation band at $55.2–57.0K almost exactly, and the close recovered to $60,089 (Kraken, Coinalyze, Nov 21).
findings.why: The question is who sold at $55K and who bought price back. The selling side was leverage: $275M of longs were liquidated on the day, close to $700M over two days with the prior day's $410M; 74% of 7-day liquidations were longs (Coinalyze, five exchanges, totals under-reported). Perps loosened afterward: OI-weighted funding is 0.08%, shorts are paying on OKX (−4.1%) and Bybit (−1.2%), and open interest is down 4.4% in 7 days. The buying side shows no spot: Coinbase, Binance and Bybit spot combined were net taker sellers of 2,906 BTC on the day, OKX spot net sold 1,284 BTC, and the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount is −0.01%. Shorts were also liquidated for $137M, 3.6x the prior day, so part of the bounce was short covering. On-chain agrees: network-wide realized loss fell from $2.84B to $1.88B (Bitview) even though price went lower intraday, so the volume at $55K was mostly in derivatives. The estimated liquidation bands then switched sides: 27.5K BTC of shorts at $65.4–67.8K above, about 8K BTC of longs at $53.7–55.1K below (multiple exchanges, estimated). The people have not left: 77.7% of Binance accounts are long, and large Hyperliquid accounts still hold more shorts (10,795 BTC) than longs (8,193 BTC).
findings.alt: The other path is that this was a mid-decline short-covering bounce: after $457M of longs were liquidated on June 2, price fell another 12% before the June 30 low. Spot tells the two apart: if Coinbase 7-day net taker flow turns positive and ETFs turn to net inflow, the covering connects to real demand; with neither, a bounce into the thick supply at $62,000–64,000 meets holders selling at breakeven. Data limits: the liquidation bands are estimated from open interest and assumed leverage and move with the assumptions; Saturday liquidity is thin, so part of the 9.8% range is a liquidity effect; lows differ by tens of dollars across exchanges.
findings.history: After a big long flush the usual pattern is a bounce, then a retest. Longs above 70% of 30-day liquidations has happened 7 times since data began in October 2022, with 5 gains after 90 days and a median of +17.7% (any day: +8.5%); the last two were Feb 5 and June 2, and the latter fell another 12% first. The 7-day funding average has turned negative 13 times since 2021, with 10 gains after 90 days; this time the 7-day average is still 2.65%, not there yet.
findings.so: What changed is the fuel for the decline: the forced long selling above $55K is cleared, so going lower needs spot sellers to push on their own, and shorts are the more crowded side above. What did not change is demand: the stablecoin and ETF outflows in yesterday's second finding are still running, so this wick only means one layer of selling pressure is gone. The $58,525 close held, and neither condition in yesterday's first finding has been met.
findings.next: By Nov 28: Coinbase spot 7-day net taker flow turning positive means real buyers arrived and this call is refuted; a close below $58,525 means nobody took over after the covering and spot sellers pushed price to a new low on their own.

check.label: Coinbase spot 7-day net taker flow turns positive

findings.title: Price bounced and protection got pricier: options do not treat $55K as the low
findings.lean_why: More money bought protection on the bounce day and puts got more expensive; the market is paying real premium for another large move soon, and what it fears is the downside.
findings.what: Price closed up 2.2%, yet options fear rose another notch: DVOL 58.0, the highest since Mar 8 (Deribit, Nov 21).
findings.why: A bounce day is usually when protection gets cheaper; this time it went the other way, so start with which part of the curve rose. The front end rose most: 7-day implied vol is 58.5%, 9.2 points above 90-day versus 7.7 the day before. The back end is repricing too: 90-day implied vol rose from 42.4% a week ago to 49.4%. Then direction: the 30-day 25Δ risk reversal is −12.7 versus −9.3 the day before, so puts gained further on calls, and buyer premium has leaned to puts for 24 days. Positioning sits below: the largest line in the Dec 4 expiry is the $58,000 put with 6,415 BTC, and the largest put in the Dec 25 expiry is at $60,000. Implied vol is 11.9 points above 30-day realized, a sizeable premium for buyers. Other markets point the same way: large Hyperliquid accounts hold more shorts than longs, and Polymarket prices a December hike at 91.6%. The contradiction is perps: funding is near zero and leverage there is no longer crowded.
findings.alt: Expensive protection can also be normal pricing for clustered events: Monday's US open, PCE on Nov 25 and the monthly expiry on Nov 27 all fall within five days, so sellers would mark up anyway. The other path is that protection has peaked and sellers start collecting premium; in that case the inversion narrows first, with the 7-day minus 90-day gap back inside 5 points. Data limits: Deribit only; open interest does not separate buyers from sellers, so the $58,000 line could also be someone selling puts for premium; the snapshot is a single post-close reading.
findings.history: DVOL in the top 2% of the past year is a first for this year, so there is no precedent to compare; the last time it was this high was 60.5 on Mar 8. Term-structure records only start Nov 6: 9 of 16 days inverted, reaching 16.1 points on Nov 14. Buyer premium has flipped to puts 7 times since November 2025, with 3 gains after 30 days and a median of −11.2%.
findings.so: What changed is how to read this bounce: perps loosened, yet more people are paying to guard against a drop, so the two markets did not turn together. The long-term valuation read is unchanged. Options only say the move will be large and the fear is to the downside; they do not point to tomorrow's direction.
findings.next: By Nov 28: DVOL back below 50 means the market treats $55K as the low of this leg and this call is refuted; DVOL above 60.5, past the March high, means fear is still widening.

followups.title: Prior low tested: this capitulation is bigger than at the June low
followups.say: Intraday low $55,100, through $58,525, with the close back at $60,089; no return above $62,000 and no close below the prior low, so neither condition is met. Deadline Nov 27.

followups.title: Buyers are leaving faster: stablecoin and ETF outflows widen together
followups.say: Stablecoins at $282.5B, only $1.5B above the $281.0B line; the 7-day change is −1.58%, with no narrowing. The Nov 20 ETF figure is a provisional −$127M with IBIT unpublished. Deadline Nov 27.

followups.title: Thin supply below the $62K close; sellers are more urgent than buyers
followups.say: Confirmed: long-term holder loss share is 46.1%, above this cycle's prior high of 45.4%, after touching 46.5% on Nov 20 (CheckOnChain); the close of $60,089 did not get back to $64,000. Price crossed the thin supply under $62K to $55K in two days.

followups.title: The 200-day MA has turned down, loosening the premise of the bull label
followups.say: 3 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA, short of 6; the close of $60,089 needs +18.5% to reach $71,201. Deadline Nov 25.

check.label: 6 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA

research.summary: No new Glassnode issue (the latest are the Nov 18 methodology piece and the Nov 17 Week On-chain; Market Pulse is due later on Nov 22). New is QCP's Nov 20 note: short-covering rallies struggle to last until tech stocks and rate volatility settle, in line with our read that spot buyers have not taken over.

items.title: QCP market note (cited in: Bitcoin rises 9% from two-year low, reclaiming $60,000 as forced selling eases)
items.points: Original not read; the following is from CoinDesk's account: BTC's next meaningful recovery needs tech stocks to stabilize, rate volatility to fall and institutional flows to return; until then, rallies driven by short covering may struggle to turn into sustained upside.
items.meaning: We see none of the three conditions yet: the Nasdaq fell 10% on the week, DVOL at 58.0 is the highest since Mar 8, and ETFs show $3.67B of net outflow over 20 trading days. Secondhand only, so not used as a basis for judgment.

items.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
items.points: 13F filers added a net 49,229 BTC equivalent in Q3 and hold a record 356,491 BTC ($29.78B), 27.6% of spot BTC funds; advisers and wealth platforms hold 40.5% of that and have bought for 9 straight quarters, while hedge funds fell from 50.6% at end-2024 to 19.0%. From quarter-end to Nov 16, fund holdings fell by 38,531 BTC.
items.meaning: Holders shifted from hedge funds to wealth-management clients who came in around $80K. Our estimated ETF holder cost is above the close, which sits 23.9% below it and has been underwater for 12 days; the definitions differ, so the figures are not netted.

items.title: CryptoQuant says bitcoin is back in a bearish phase but has reached a 'value zone'
items.points: The original report is blocked (403); the following is from The Block's account: BTC is below the 200-day MA at $72,900 and the 365-day MA at $75,900; 30-day demand growth is under −400K BTC, the fastest contraction since July 1; Bull Score 10/100; trader unrealized loss of −20% marks a 'value zone', but such bottoms usually take at least two months; a sustained break of $62,000–65,000 would weaken the zone.
items.meaning: Its $62,000 has now been broken on the close for three days, with an intraday low of $55,100. Cheap but needing time matches our read: the Dawn Index is in Deep Night and the weekly bull-bear score is negative. Its demand measure is computed differently from our apparent demand; the direction is the same.

items.title: Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?
items.points: ETFs took in a net $6.36B in Q3 at a flow-weighted entry near $78,300; Q4 through Nov 17 saw $3.09B leave. Holding below $61,300 with a single-day ETF outflow above $300M points to the July 1 low of $57,803; three straight days of ETF inflows and STH-SOPR back at 1 would open $69,400 and $72,700.
items.meaning: Its $57,803 was broken intraday, with a low of $55,100, and the close came back to $60,089. None of its conditions for a turn has appeared: ETFs are still leaving and STH-SOPR is 0.966, below 1 for 16 days.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Capitulation Meets Support
items.points: BTC fell to $62K on Nov 15 with realized losses back at levels seen only near the 2018, 2020 and 2022 lows; $62–66K holds about a fifth of short-term holder supply; the remaining long-liquidation band sits at $59.5–62.2K; reclaiming $74.1K would look like a base, while a daily close below $62K points to $58.5K and the realized price at $53.7K.
items.meaning: Its $58.5K was broken intraday and held on the close, with the close still 11.5% above its next stop, the realized price; our Bitview realized price is $53,206. The short-term supply at $62–66K is now entirely underwater and is the first layer of breakeven selling on any bounce.

items.title: No gain, plenty of pain
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC fell 14% on the week, a sixth straight red week, with daily RSI below 20; stablecoins saw $16.1B of net redemptions in a month, the most since the Terra collapse; ETF exposure is back to mid-August, option skew shows heavy hedging and funding is negative, all of which it says have marked BTC bottoms before.
items.meaning: It reads stablecoin redemptions as bottom evidence; we read them as buyers not yet back: DefiLlama shows $19.0B gone in 30 days, still accelerating a week later. The conditions in yesterday's second finding will settle which reading holds.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 47
items.points: BTC fell about 13% on the week; futures open interest dropped 7.2% to $34.2B, the lowest since August; 25Δ skew 13.7%; weekly ETF outflow $995M; its conclusion was that leverage had been flushed and the market was less crowded.
items.meaning: Less crowded only became roughly accurate a week late: after another round of long liquidations this week, our weighted funding is near zero and open interest is down 4.4% in 7 days. The next Market Pulse is due later on Nov 22.

cards.dawn: Bullish on the long view: heat has dropped into the night zone, with unrealized profit at a 4-year low. But the weekly score is negative for a 2nd week; 2 more and it flips bearish.
cards.avgd: Bullish: price sits unusually far below the nine cost lines, with the 200-week average the most stretched. Cheap is a zone, though: after the 2014 entry price still fell another 46.6%.
cards.p20: Bullish long term: MVRV is a small fraction of the last cycle peak, and price would need about +85% to reach the 0.75 line. Pi Cycle and the top radar are far off too; the live question is the bottom.
cards.lthloss: Leaning bullish, at the edge: the long-term holder loss share sits just under this cycle's high, inside past bear-bottom ranges. A close below about $58,500 sets a new high and breaks the pattern.
cards.cyccmp: Neutral: this cycle is down about half from its top while past cycles were below -75% by the same day. The old timetable does not fit, so the 847-1,177 days to regain the top may not apply.
cards.levels: Bearish: the close is below the true market mean of $76,327, so active investors are underwater, ETF buyers too. Below, only the realized price at $53.2K is left as a line.
cards.urpd: Neutral with overhead supply: 927K BTC sit at 62K-64K waiting to break even, and the next big pile below is far lower. Nearly all coins that moved in 7 days moved at a loss.
cards.strike: Neutral: the 12/25 expiry holds nearly 40% of open interest, calls massed at $80,000 and puts at $60,000, right where price sits. Gamma is negative below, so a break would amplify moves.
cards.legs: Bearish: this down leg is already deeper than 9 in 10 of the last 12, yet it only ends on a close back at $67,627. Price sits at the low edge of value, below the $63,750 volume node.
cards.pullback: Bearish: three of the pressure lights have been on together for 22 days, and past runs like this saw a small median loss 90 days later. Pressure eases only when two of the three clear.
cards.profit: Bullish: over nine in ten recent buyers are underwater, and past readings above 60% rose 30 days later 12 of 16 times. The share is off its 11/20 peak; the worst may be passing.
cards.sopr: Bearish: recent buyers have sold at a loss for 16 straight days, deeper than the late-October dip, with realized profit a small fraction of losses. A move back above 1 ends the handover.
cards.rpl: Bearish, in a bottom zone but unconfirmed: the one-year profit/loss ratio is still at its low, and 7-day losses run about 9x profits. Past rebounds to 0.81 never saw a new price low.
cards.miners: Bearish: price is below the $65,658 power breakeven for mainstream rigs and under 1% above production cost, while hashrate and difficulty keep rising. Hash Ribbons have not capitulated yet.
cards.etf: Bearish: spot ETFs keep bleeding, this run is 12x what miners mined meanwhile, and the 20-day total is in an outflow phase. Strategy sits 20% under its cost; no institutional buyer is stepping in.
cards.pr-us: Neutral: net of the USDT discount, US demand matches offshore; the headline negative premium is mostly USDT trading under $1. Asian OTC buyers are keener, paying a +0.77% premium.
cards.ad: Bearish: apparent demand is negative over 30 days and a year, realized cap has had no new money for 8 days, and stablecoins shrank $19B in a month. Rallies lack fresh buyers until 30-day demand turns.
cards.whale: Bearish: both whale tiers are cutting this month, with the 1K-10K tier selling fastest this week. Long-term holders have been net sellers for 109 days, shifting coins to short-term hands.
cards.svd: Neutral: OKX taker buys only slightly lead over 7 days and sellers led the latest day. Large orders are selling and Coinbase spot is unusually heavy, so one venue's small net buying proves little.
cards.stk: Bearish: BTC has fallen more than twice as much as Nasdaq in two months, and their 30-day correlation is 0.66. Bonds and prediction markets price a hike; a weak Monday open leaves BTC little room.
cards.fh: Neutral: longs were flushed hard at 55K and funding is low but still positive. Nearly 80% of Binance accounts still lean long, so the retail flush is incomplete until funding turns negative.
cards.vol: Neutral: implied vol is near a one-year high, well above realized, and front months cost more than back months. Expect bigger swings around Monday's open; direction hinges on 58,525.
cards.oi: Bearish: option buyers have favored puts for 24 days and risk reversals price puts richer, so money is in downside protection. Max pain for 12/25 sits 20% above, but its pull is weak.
cards.fng: Bearish but near an extreme: sentiment fell from greed to extreme fear within a month, and first drops into extreme fear usually saw lower prices 30 days on. Recovery means back above 25.
